title: Physics-based differentiable imaging detects 51 Eridani b in a JWST band where standard processing did not
summary: A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection. The paper also reports two- to fifteen-fold sensitivity gains across its test observations.
ai_technology: FLIP (Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets), a differentiable instrument model optimized with automatic differentiation
organization: Northwestern University; California Institute of Technology; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Space Telescope Science Institute

evidence.tested: A physics-based coronagraph model optimized with automatic differentiation and gradient descent recovered 51 Eridani b in JWST/NIRCam F430M images at 4.3 μm, where the published standard-processing result was a non-detection.
evidence.unknown: The planet 51 Eridani b was already discovered by ground-based imaging in 2015; the new finding is its first JWST image in the 4.3 μm carbon-dioxide band, not discovery of a previously unknown planet. Performance estimates are based on a limited set of three target systems and should not be generalized to all JWST data.
evidence.ai_role: Optimized telescope aberration and detector parameters against the observed JWST point-spread function to subtract starlight; this image analysis recovered a 6.3σ signal at 4.3 μm in a dataset whose original analysis reported no detection.
